messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on hosted last night after we flipped the new kernel selector + microbatcher tuning. p95 up ~30% and p99 doubled for long-context (>=2k) traces. we should decide on immediate mitigations (timeouts / truncation / caps) and a longer-term mitigation (kernel selectors + kv cache behavior).
Mira: ouch. can you paste the dashboard snippet? which pool/region?
Alex: east-1 rtx-pool. from the dashboard:
- baseline (before): p50 45ms, p95 170ms, p99 600ms
- after change:   p50 48ms, p95 220ms, p99 1200ms
correlation: change rolled at 02:12, spike starts 02:20, sustained until rollback at 05:00.
Sam: likely culprit: selector now prefers new 4-bit matmul kernel for throughput but it regresses on long seq due to cache-unfriendly tiling. microbatcher also increased target batch size from 8→16 for seq>512 which amplifies tail. we saw similar last year.
Jordan: short term: we can protect the SLO by (a) tightening microbatch max for long sequences, (b) applying a soft max_tokens cap per-call for hosted tiers, and (c) enforce a truncation-from-left policy for prompts over N tokens. which of these do we want as immediate safety nets?
Linh: +1 to microbatch cap. also KV cache: when we truncate we saw more KV churn because session ids mismatch and clients resend prefixes. propose a TTL-based eviction for idle sessions and avoid full KV eviction on truncation; instead mark truncated prefixes and reuse suffix caches when possible.
Mira: what about timeouts? we could reduce "max_generation_time" to 3s for non-SLA plans; that would kill some long tails but could impact completeness.
Alex: agree. rough plan for a 2-hour mitigation window:
1) set microbatch max_size=8 for seq_len>=1024
2) set per-request soft max_tokens=1024 for hosted free/standard tiers (enterprise unchanged)
3) set generation timeout 3s for same tiers
4) apply left-truncation policy when prompt_len + expected_gen > 2048
5) telemetry: add tracing tag kernel=active_selector and microbatch_size to all traces

Mira: canary config snippet (for eng-runtime canary A):
```
routes:
  - matcher: "pool:rtx-east-1 && seq_len >= 1024"
    microbatch:
      max_size: 8
    runtime:
      generation_timeout_ms: 3000
      max_tokens_soft: 1024
    truncation:
      strategy: left-truncate
      preserve_prompt_tokens: 512
```
Sam: for longer term: we need to improve kernel scoring heuristics to include seq_len and kv_cache_hit_ratio, not just base throughput. also add a fallback to verified kernels whenever p99 > threshold for a route.
Jordan: +1. also propose a token-shedding policy: drop the earliest assistant messages with low importance when token budget exceeded. low-effort but high-impact on tail.
Linh: profiling notes: I ran nvprof on a problematic trace — kernel matmul time grows superlinearly after 2k tokens because of cache thrash. KV cache lookups also spike at truncation boundaries. attaching snippet in the evals run (saved to s3).
Alex: deploy-bot can we schedule a canary rollout now with Mira's config and watch p99? aim is p99 < 900ms within 30 minutes of canary.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled for rtx-east-1 at 09:30 UTC. will report back on health and p95/p99 every 5m.
ops-bot: alerting rule temporarily adjusted: p99 "long-context" > 1.0s for 3 consecutive windows triggers page.
Mira: quick question — should the soft max_tokens be enforced at the gateway or at the runtime? gateway prevents wasted routing but runtime can do smarter truncation.
Sam: do both: gateway should enforce hard rejects/soft caps for cost control; runtime should accept and apply truncation strategy so we don't break model input expectations.
Jordan: rollout plan summary: canary -> monitor 30m -> if p99 < 900ms and errors < 0.5% promote. if not, rollback selector and keep microbatch cap + truncation enabled.
Alex: assigned actions:
- Mira: push canary config + dashboard panel for kernel tag (in 30m)
- Sam: sketch kernel selector scoring update (include kv hit ratio) and a verified-kernel fallback (EOD)
- Linh: add TTL eviction PR and validate no owner-sensitive KV leaks (today)
- Jordan: draft customer messaging for enterprise customers + default policy notes (today)
- Ops: monitor canary and be ready to rollback (oncall)

Mira: noted, starting canary now. will post back with first 10m metrics. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks all — prioritize SLO protection over throughput for this window. we'll iterate on smarter routing after we stabilise.
prio-bot: priority set to P0 for this thread and assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
Mira: first 10m snapshot: p95 back to ~175ms, p99 ~760ms, error rate +0.1%. holding.
Sam: nice. looks like microbatch cap + truncation did most of the heavy lifting. kernel selector still causes a small tail; feel free to leave verified-kernel fallback in prod until selector improvements land.
Alex: ok let's keep this config for 24h and then reopen for deeper perf analysis (profiling and kernel scoring). thanks everyone.
